name: Cessna 340/414/421
summary: Family of pressurized cabin-class piston twins used by owner-pilots, charter and small freight operators.

wings: Low straight wing; tip tanks on the 340 and early 414/421, plain tips on 414A/421C
engines: Two flat-six engines in long nacelles with baggage lockers at the rear
fuselage: Portly, round-section pressurized cabin with small rounded windows
Airstair door at the rear on the left (414/421)

tellTales: Portly round-section cabin with small porthole-like windows on a piston twin
Long nacelles extending behind the wing

confusedWith.howToTell: The 310 has a slim unpressurized fuselage with large rectangular windows; the 340/414/421 is fatter with smaller rounded windows.
The Navajo has large square windows and a less-rounded fuselage; the Cessna has small rounded windows on a round pressurized cabin.
The King Air has turboprop nacelles with exhaust stacks; the 340/414/421 have piston cowlings with no stacks.
The Conquest has turboprop cowlings with big spinners and a larger, longer fuselage; the 340/414/421 has piston engines with stub exhausts and a slightly smaller airframe.
The 402 is unpressurized with a long, straight-sided cabin and larger windows; the 340/414/421 have a portly pressurized cabin with small porthole-like windows.
The Duke has plain wingtips, a smooth round fuselage and a swept fin without a dorsal fillet; the 340 is portly with a dorsal fillet and, on early models, tip tanks.
